Contributing to anndataR

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for your interest in contributing to anndataR! Contributions of all kinds are welcome, including bug reports, documentation improvements and code.

Reporting issues and asking questions

Please use the issue tracker and pick the matching template.

Contributing code

  1. Open an issue first for anything larger than a small fix
  2. Fork the repository and create a branch from devel
  3. Make your changes, following the conventions below
  4. Open a pull request against devel and fill in the PR template

Conventions

  • Format code with Air (air format .) and vignettes with styler::style_dir("vignettes"), then check with lintr::lint_package()
  • Document functions with roxygen2 and regenerate the man pages with devtools::document(), using the roxygen2 version pinned in DESCRIPTION (Config/roxygen2/version)
  • Add or update tests in tests/testthat/
  • Add or update examples in the vignettes where relevant
  • Check that new behaviour matches Python anndata where applicable (see the roundtrip tests)
  • Keep lines to 120 characters or fewer (use paste() to wrap long strings in tests)
  • Use check_requires() before using an optional package and add a matching skip in tests
  • Use cli for messages and errors

Running checks

devtools::test()
devtools::test(filter = "roundtrip-X")  # Run a single test file
devtools::check()
BiocCheck::BiocCheck()

Some tests require Python anndata and are skipped if it is not available. Set ANNDATAR_TEST_REQUIRE_PYTHON=true to make them fail instead.

Testing

  • Use the skip_if_no_*() helpers in tests/testthat/ for tests needing optional dependencies (Python anndata, dummy_anndata, zarr, h5diff)
  • Use generate_dataset() to create mock data with different matrix types and edge cases
  • Add a roundtrip test (test-roundtrip-*.R) when changing anything that affects compatibility with Python
  • Verify HDF5 changes against Python output with h5diff

Package design

See the software design article for details. Some key points to be aware of:

  • AnnData classes: AbstractAnnData is the base class for InMemoryAnnData, HDF5AnnData, ZarrAnnData, ReticulateAnnData and AnnDataView. Changes to the interface usually need to be made in all of them.
  • Names are stored separately: obs_names and var_names are stored apart from obs/var, and dimnames are added when data is accessed. Internal code should use adata$obs_names and adata$var_names rather than rownames(adata$obs) or colnames(adata$X).
  • Views are read-only: AnnDataView (returned by adata[i, j]) subsets lazily and can’t be modified. Convert it with one of the $as_*AnnData() methods first when needed.
  • Validation: setters use the validation helpers in AbstractAnnData. Update these if you change the rules for a slot.
  • Conversion: from_*() functions convert other formats to AnnData and as_*() functions convert AnnData to other formats. Update both when adding a conversion feature.
  • Python differences: Python AnnData allows duplicate names and distinguishes None from an empty dict, which R doesn’t. Known issues are tracked in inst/known_issues.yaml.

Package authors

New contributors are welcome to add themselves to the package authors in DESCRIPTION. Add a person() entry with the ctb role in your pull request, including your ORCID and GitHub username in the comment field.

Code of conduct

Please be respectful and constructive in all interactions. This project follows the scverse code of conduct.
